name: Therese Johaug
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze medal in 30km classical at the 2007 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Sapporo at age 18, followed by three golds at the 2008 Junior World Championships and Olympic gold in the 4x5km relay at Vancouver 2010.
early_history_summary: Johaug grew up in the small village of Dalsbygda in Os Municipality, Norway, and began skiing locally as a child. She joined the Tynset ski club when she started gymnasium and made her World Cup debut in January 2007 at age 18, quickly earning a spot at the World Championships where she won bronze.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian national team pipeline, cross-country skiing culture, early international competition
evidence_summary: Johaug emerged from a small Norwegian village into the dominant cross-country skiing nation's national team pipeline by age 18, winning a World Championship bronze in her first senior championship. Norway's deep cross-country skiing culture and structured national team development provided the ecosystem for her rapid rise. No family background details are documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in the small village of Dalsbygda in Os Municipality, Norway; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive cross-country skiing after the 2022 Olympics; one of the most decorated female cross-country skiers in history with 4 Olympic golds and 14 World Championship golds; married Nils Jakob Hoff in 2023.

trajectory.event: Won bronze in 30km classical at the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Sapporo.

name: Mark Messier

early_history_summary: Messier grew up in a hockey family in St. Albert, Alberta; his father Doug was a professional hockey player who coached and mentored him. He started playing at age 4, made the AJHL at 15, played in the WHA at 17-18, and entered the NHL with the Edmonton Oilers at 19 in 1979.

He played junior hockey at 15, turned professional in the WHA at 17, and entered the NHL at 19 with the Edmonton Oilers. By 21 he scored 50 goals and by 23 won his first Stanley Cup, benefiting from the Oilers dynasty and partnership with Wayne Gretzky.
starting_point: Born in St. Albert, Alberta, Canada; father Doug Messier was a professional hockey player who coached and mentored Mark from childhood.
current_position: Retired from the NHL in 2004 after 25 seasons; inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2007; widely considered one of the greatest hockey players of all time with 6 Stanley Cups and 1887 career points.

name: Ferdinand Bracke

early_history_summary: Bracke was born in Hamme, Belgium and moved to Wallonia as an infant, learning French early. He worked in a factory while training as an amateur cyclist, winning a stage of the Peace Race in 1962 before his breakthrough at the Grand Prix des Nations.
family_context_summary: Born in Hamme, East Flanders, Belgium; family emigrated to Wallonia when he was one year old; worked in a factory while training as an amateur cyclist.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Belgian cycling culture, time trial specialist, factory worker background, Peugeot team
evidence_summary: Bracke emerged from Belgium's deep cycling culture, working factory shifts while training as an amateur. His time trial talent was evident early, winning the prestigious Grand Prix des Nations at 23 as an amateur against professionals. He turned pro with Peugeot and became world pursuit champion at 25, benefiting from Belgium's position as a cycling frontier.
starting_point: Born in Hamme, East Flanders, Belgium in 1939; family emigrated to Wallonia when he was one year old; worked in a factory while training as an amateur cyclist.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling in 1978; best known for the World Hour Record (1967) and winning the 1971 Vuelta a España.

name: Inger Aufles
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship silver in the 3x5km relay at the 1966 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Oslo at age 25, then won Olympic gold in the relay and bronze in the 10km at the 1968 Grenoble Olympics at age 26.
early_history_summary: Aufles was born in Valldal, Norway, and moved to Mosjøen in northern Norway at age 20 where she married and began systematic training with Kjærstad IL. She made the national team in 1966 and quickly became one of Norway's leading female cross-country skiers.
family_context_summary: Born in Valldal, Norway; moved to Mosjøen at age 20, married, and began systematic cross-country skiing training with Kjærstad IL.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian cross-country skiing culture, national team, late start at 20, relay team
evidence_summary: Aufles began serious skiing training only at 20 after moving to northern Norway, but within five years made the national team and won World Championship silver. At 26 she won Olympic gold in the relay at Grenoble. Norway's dominant cross-country skiing culture and national team pipeline accelerated her late-start career.
starting_point: Born in Valldal, Norway in 1941; moved to Mosjøen in northern Norway at age 20 where she married and began systematic cross-country skiing training with Kjærstad IL.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing after the 1972 season; lives in Norway; one of the early stars of Norwegian women's cross-country skiing.

trajectory.event: Selected for the Norwegian national team and won World Championship silver in the relay in Oslo.

name: Liya Kebede
milestone_by_age_26: Featured on the cover of Paris Vogue in May 2002 at age 24 with the entire issue dedicated to her; became the first woman of color to be named the face of Estée Lauder in 2003 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Kebede was born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and attended the French international Lycée Guébré-Mariam where a film director spotted her and introduced her to a modeling agent. She moved to Paris after school, struggled initially, then relocated to Chicago before her break with Tom Ford's Gucci in 2000.
family_context_summary: Born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; father was an airline executive and mother worked in public relations; grew up affluent by Ethiopian standards; only daughter among four brothers.
primary_early_advantage_tags: French international school, film director discovery, Tom Ford Gucci exclusive, diversity in fashion
evidence_summary: Kebede was spotted at a French international school in Addis Ababa by a film director who connected her to a Parisian modeling agent. Her affluent family background (father an airline executive) enabled attendance at the French lycée and international mobility. Her big break came when Tom Ford selected her for a Gucci exclusive at 22, leading to a Paris Vogue cover at 24 and the Estée Lauder contract at 25.
starting_point: Born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia in 1978; father was an airline executive and mother worked in public relations; grew up affluent by Ethiopian standards and attended the French international Lycée Guébré-Mariam.
current_position: Ethiopian supermodel, actress, and clothing designer; founder of lemlem clothing line supporting Ethiopian artisans; WHO Goodwill Ambassador; has appeared on 20 Vogue covers.

name: Maurizio Cattelan
milestone_by_age_26: Worked various manual jobs (gardener, cook, postal worker, morgue worker) and made furniture through his twenties; first solo art exhibition was in 1989 at age 29. No material milestone by 26 found.

He had no formal art training and began making art in the late 1980s.
family_context_summary: Born in Padua, Italy; father was a truck driver, mother was a cleaning lady; family struggled financially; mother died when Cattelan was in his early twenties.

early_history_summary: Grigoraș was born in Satu Mare, Romania and began gymnastics at age 6 in Onesti under Maria Cosma and Mihai Agoston. She trained at CSS Cetate Deva with the Károlyi system, making the national team by her early teens and competing at the Olympics at 14.
family_context_summary: Born in Satu Mare, Romania; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Romanian gymnastics system, Károlyi coaching, Deva training center, Olympic team at 14
evidence_summary: Grigoraș entered Romania's elite gymnastics pipeline at age 6, training at the famed CSS Cetate Deva under Béla and Márta Károlyi. She made the Olympic team at 14, winning silver in Moscow, and became European champion on vault at 15. The Romanian gymnastics system provided world-class coaching, facilities, and peer training with Nadia Comăneci and other elites.
starting_point: Born in Satu Mare, Romania in 1966; began gymnastics at age 6 in Onesti under coaches Maria Cosma and Mihai Agoston.
current_position: Retired Romanian gymnast; two-time Olympic medalist (team gold 1984, silver 1980) and four-time European Championship medalist in 1981; a balance beam skill is named after her.

name: Peter Leko
milestone_by_age_26: Became the world's youngest chess grandmaster in history in January 1994 at age 14 years and 4 months, breaking the record previously held by Judit Polgár; challenged for the Classical World Chess Championship in 2004 at age 25, drawing 7-7 with Vladimir Kramnik.
early_history_summary: Leko was born in Subotica, Yugoslavia to an ethnic Hungarian family and moved to Szeged, Hungary at age one. His father taught him chess at age seven, and he began tournament play at nine. He earned the IM title at 12 and became the youngest GM ever at 14, studying chess full-time from childhood.
family_context_summary: Born in Subotica, Yugoslavia to an ethnic Hungarian family; moved to Szeged, Hungary at age one; lived with his mother, grandmother, and brother; father taught him chess at age seven.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father taught him chess shortly before age seven, initiating his path in the game; no further family domain expertise documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: chess from age 7, full-time study, Hungarian chess tradition, youngest GM record, sustained coaching
evidence_summary: Leko learned chess from his father at age seven and began full-time study and tournament play by nine, supported by coaches Tibor Károlyi and later András Adorján. He became the youngest grandmaster in history at 14, breaking Judit Polgár's record. Hungary's strong chess tradition and access to elite European tournaments facilitated his rapid rise. He lived modestly with his mother and grandmother in Szeged.
starting_point: Born in Subotica, Yugoslavia to an ethnic Hungarian family; moved to Szeged, Hungary at age one; lived with his mother, grandmother, and brother; father taught him chess at age seven.
current_position: Retired from top-level competitive chess; works as a chess commentator and analyst; former world championship challenger who peaked at world No. 4.
